title: Passage ranking and document chunking
summary: Google says passage ranking is an AI system it uses to identify individual sections or passages of a web page to better understand how relevant the page is to a search. RAG vendors separately document chunking: Microsoft says splitting large documents helps stay under model token limits and prevents truncation loss, suggests starting at 512 tokens with 25% overlap, and notes that HTML or Markdown headings can be used to chunk by section. Vendor chunk sizes describe that vendor's tooling only; none of them is a Google rule.
actions: Give long pages clear headings and self-contained sections; this is practitioner inference from Google's passage statement.
Do not copy Azure's 512-token figure as a target for web pages.
If you build RAG, chunk to stay under embedding limits and use headings where possible.
Do not split one page into many thin URLs on the strength of passage ranking alone.

myths.myth: Passage ranking means Google ranks separate pieces of your page as separate results.
myths.correction: Google describes it as identifying passages to better understand how relevant the page is.

myths.myth: Azure's recommended chunk size is the size Google uses.
myths.correction: It is Azure AI Search guidance for building RAG indexes.

items.prompt: Google says passage ranking identifies individual sections or "___" of a web page. Fill the blank with the one word in quotation marks.
items.explanation: Google says passage ranking is an AI system used to identify individual sections or "passages" of a web page.

items.prompt: What chunk size and overlap does Microsoft recommend starting with for Azure AI Search?
options: A. 128 tokens with no overlap between chunks
B. 512 tokens with 25% overlap
C. 8,191 tokens with 50% overlap between chunks
D. 50 tokens with 10% overlap between chunks
items.explanation: Correct: Azure recommends starting with 512 tokens (about 2,000 characters) and an initial 25% overlap. Wrong: '128 tokens with no overlap' - 128 tokens is the size of the overlap, not the chunk. '8,191 tokens with 50% overlap' - 8,191 is an example embedding input limit. '50 tokens with 10% overlap' - not a figure Azure gives in the saved quote.

items.prompt: True or false: Microsoft's Azure documentation says chunking is required for every document regardless of its size.
items.explanation: The page says chunking is only required if source documents are too large for the model's maximum input size, though it can also help if content is poorly represented as a single vector.

items.prompt: Microsoft says partitioning content into chunks helps meet input requirements and prevents data loss due to what?
items.explanation: The documentation says chunking prevents data loss due to truncation when text exceeds model input limits.

items.prompt: A colleague says 'Passage ranking means Google ranks parts of my page as separate results.' Which correction is best?
options: A. Google ranks only the first paragraph of each page it indexes
B. Azure chunking replaced Google's passage ranking system
C. Passages remove the need for the page to be indexed first
D. Google uses passages to better judge how relevant a page is to a search
items.explanation: Correct: Google describes identifying passages to better understand how relevant the page is to a search. Wrong: 'Google ranks only the first paragraph' - not stated. 'Passage ranking was replaced by Azure chunking' - Azure is a different vendor's tool. 'Passages replace the need for indexing' - not stated.

items.prompt: Which statement is NOT supported by the saved sources?
options: A. Google says passage ranking identifies sections of a page
B. Azure says HTML or Markdown headings can be used to chunk by section
C. Google ranks passages of exactly 512 tokens with a 25% overlap between them
D. Azure cites 8,191 tokens as the input limit of text-embedding-3-small
items.explanation: Supported: Google's passage ranking identifies sections (A); Azure says HTML/Markdown headings can chunk by section (B); Azure gives 8,191 tokens as one model's limit (D). Unsupported: C - Azure's 512-token figure is its own guidance, not Google's passage size.

items.prompt: Hypothetical internal RAG index: you keep Azure's suggested 25% overlap but use 1,024-token chunks. How many tokens does the overlap contain? Answer with the number.
items.explanation: Azure's starting recommendation is 512-token chunks with a 25% overlap (128 tokens). Applying 25% to 1,024-token chunks gives 256 tokens. This is arithmetic on a hypothetical setup; whether 1,024 tokens suits your content is not claimed.

items.prompt: A strategist writes: 'Azure recommends 512-token chunks, so Google ranks 512-token passages; make every section 512 tokens.' What is the error?
options: A. Vendor RAG guidance is presented as if it were a rule for Google's ranking
B. Azure never mentions a chunk size anywhere in its documentation
C. Google's passage ranking system does not exist at all
D. Every section must be exactly 8,191 tokens long to be indexed
items.explanation: Correct: a vendor's RAG guidance is applied to a different system; Google gives no such size in the saved quote. Wrong: 'Azure never mentions chunk size' - it does. 'Passage ranking does not exist' - Google describes it. 'Sections must be 8,191 tokens' - that is a model input limit example.

items.prompt: Hypothetical site: a long buying guide on one URL with clear H2 sections. Symptom: a manager wants it split into twelve thin URLs 'so each part ranks'. Evidence: (1) Google says passage ranking identifies sections of a page to understand relevance; (2) no saved source says splitting is needed; (3) Azure's heading-based chunking is for RAG indexes. Question: what is the best course?
options: A. Split into twelve thin URLs because Azure chunks documents
B. Keep one page with clear H2 sections and test before splitting anything
C. Remove all headings so Google sees one single block of text
D. Double the length of the guide so every section is longer
items.explanation: Correct: keep one page with clear sections, since Google says it can look at sections of a page; splitting is not shown to be needed (practitioner inference). Wrong: 'Split because Azure chunks documents' - Azure guidance is not Google's. 'Remove headings to avoid chunks' - headings help structure. 'Double the page length' - not supported.

items.prompt: Hypothetical team: an internal search assistant. Symptom: answers about the end of long manuals are missing. Evidence: (1) whole manuals of about 20,000 tokens are embedded as one input; (2) the embedding model's limit is 8,191 tokens; (3) Azure says exceeding the limit risks truncation. Question: what is the best fix?
options: A. Raise the Google crawl rate for the documentation site
B. Add special schema to all of the manuals before embedding
C. Chunk the manuals so each piece stays under the limit
D. Embed only the titles of the manuals instead of their text
items.explanation: Correct: chunk the manuals into smaller pieces (for example, headings or fixed sizes with overlap) so each stays under the limit. Wrong: 'Raise the Google crawl rate' - unrelated to embedding input. 'Add special schema' - unrelated. 'Embed only titles' - loses the content.
